tools.description: Execute a shell command synchronously or in the background

env.description: Extra environment variables, e.g. {"PYTHONPATH": "/testbed"}. Added to the existing environment rather than replacing it. Prefer this over a 'KEY=value cmd' prefix: values needing quotes or spaces are handled correctly.

max_output_bytes.description: Total captured bytes per output stream. Larger output is truncated per truncate_mode.

stdin.description: Data to feed the command on standard input, then close it. Lets you run 'python -', 'patch -p1', or 'sh -s' without first writing a temporary file.

tail.description: Return only the last N lines of each stream. Applied after the byte budget, so if the command produced more than max_output_bytes these are the last N lines of what was captured. Setting this makes the capture keep the tail of the output (truncate_mode T1) unless you name a mode yourself.

truncate_mode.description: How to divide the byte budget when output is too long: "H<n>T<n>" with weights for the head and tail sections. H2T3 keeps the first 40% and last 60%; T1 keeps only the tail (useful for build/test errors); H1 keeps only the beginning.

tools.name: shell

tools.description: Manage background processes: read bounded output snapshots or kill

action.description: read: get current bounded output snapshot. kill: terminate.

tail.description: Return only the last N lines from each stream (read only). Applied to what the process captured, which was bounded by the max_output_bytes and truncate_mode given when it was started.

tools.name: process

tools.description: View or edit files. command=view reads a file or range; command=str_replace requires old_str and new_str; command=insert requires insert_line and insert_text; command=write requires file_text and creates or overwrites the full file.

command.description: Command to execute: view, str_replace, insert, or write

file_text.description: Required for write. Full file content; creates or overwrites the file.

insert_line.description: Required for insert. Line number to insert after; use 0 to insert at the start.

insert_text.description: Required for insert. Text to insert.

max_output_bytes.description: Total bytes of output to return. Larger output is truncated per truncate_mode.

old_str.description: Required for str_replace. Text to find; must match exactly once.

truncate_mode.description: How to divide the byte budget when output is too long: "H<n>T<n>" with weights for the head and tail sections. H2T3 keeps the first 40% and last 60%; T1 keeps only the tail (useful for errors at the end); H1 keeps only the beginning.

view_range.description: For view only: [start, end] inclusive line range.

tools.name: text_editor

tools.description: Search files using ripgrep with a regex pattern

limit.description: Maximum number of matching lines to return globally

max_output_bytes.description: Total bytes of output to return. Larger output is truncated per truncate_mode.

truncate_mode.description: How to divide the byte budget when output is too long: "H<n>T<n>" with weights for the head and tail sections. H2T3 keeps the first 40% and last 60%; T1 keeps only the tail (useful for errors at the end); H1 keeps only the beginning.

tools.name: grep_files

tools.description: Fetch a URL and return its content in the specified format

max_output_bytes.description: Total bytes of output to return. Larger output is truncated per truncate_mode.

timeout.description: Request timeout in seconds. Values are clamped to the runtime maximum.

tools.description: Search the web and return results from multiple engines

max_results.description: Maximum results. Values are clamped to the runtime maximum.

tools.name: web_search

tools.description: Ensure a file with the given sha256 exists locally, downloading from a URL if not cached. Returns the local path.

sha256.description: Optional expected sha256 hex digest; when set, download fails if the content does not match

url.description: HTTP(S) URL to download the artifact from if not cached

tools.name: artifact

tools.description: Observe asynchronous sandbox facts. Delivery is opt-in: action=subscribe registers interest in event kinds (optionally narrowed to specific sources) so they arrive with later tool responses; action=wait (the default) blocks until a matching event occurs or the timeout elapses. Events expire automatically after their time-to-live.

action.description: wait: block for a matching event. subscribe: receive these kinds with later tool responses (nothing is delivered without a subscription). unsubscribe: stop receiving them. subscriptions: list active ones.

include_own.description: Also receive events caused by your own tool calls. Off by default: your call's result already reported them.

kinds.description: Event kinds, e.g. ["process_exited", "tool:text_editor", "tool:web_fetch"]. Any tool call is observable as "tool:<name>". Required for subscribe; omit when waiting to accept any kind.

sources.description: Wait only for events from these handles: a pid returned by a background shell call, or a file path. Omit to accept any source. Use this to wait on one specific background process.

timeout.description: Seconds to wait before giving up. Clamped to the runtime maximum.

tools.name: wait_for_events
